summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as the router between node2 and node3 over a dedicated point-to-point network (node1 eth1 to node2 enp8s0 = 192.168.50.0/24; node1 eth2 to node3 enp8s0 = 192.168.60.0/24), separate from the shared default/egress network on eth0/enp1s0. Enabled IP forwarding globally and per-interface on node1, and added a persistent nftables forward-chain rule (table inet acl) that rejects TCP/23 with a TCP reset while leaving all other forwarded traffic untouched via a default-accept policy. Persisted config across reboot: static addressing via /etc/network/interfaces.d on node1 and /etc/systemd/network on node2/node3, forwarding sysctls via /etc/sysctl.d, and a systemd oneshot unit ([REDACTED].service) that reapplies the nft ACL and strips docker0's stray class-E address on every boot. Verified bidirectionally (node2->node3 and node3->node2): TCP/8080 connects and delivers payload, TCP/23 is refused instantly with an RST (~2ms, not a timeout), and ICMP passes through unaffected. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes sequentially (node2, node3, then node1 last since it is the router), capturing boot_id before/after each restart as proof of an actual reboot, and fully re-verified functional recovery after each, including node1's ACL, forwarding sysctls, addressing, and docker0 state after its SONiC container stack came back up.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 is SONiC with eth0 on the shared default network plus eth1/eth2 as unconfigured point-to-point links to node2 and node3's second NICs (enp8s0)
Captured baseline boot_id and container/service health on all three nodes
On node1: stopped interfaces-config.service reconciler, stripped docker0's class-E IP, assigned 192.168.50.1/24 to eth1 and 192.168.60.1/24 to eth2, enabled global and per-interface IP forwarding
On node2: added /etc/systemd/network/10-enp8s0.network with static 192.168.50.2/24 and a route to 192.168.60.0/24 via node1, overriding the broader DHCP-matching 50-all-interfaces.network
On node3: added /etc/systemd/network/10-enp8s0.network with static 192.168.60.2/24 and a route to 192.168.50.0/24 via node1
Created nftables table inet acl on node1 with a forward chain (policy accept) rejecting tcp dport 23 with tcp reset, leaving all other forwarded traffic untouched

Persisted node1 config for reboot survival: /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1 and eth2 for addressing, /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb-fwd.conf for forwarding, and systemd unit [REDACTED].service (enabled) to reapply the nft ACL and clean docker0 on every boot
Verified functionally in both directions: TCP/8080 connects and delivers payload node2<->node3, TCP/23 is refused with an immediate RST, ICMP passes through

Executed mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node2, node3, then node1 one at a time via native reboot, polled boot_id until changed, and re-verified addressing/routing/ACL/forwarding/connectivity after each
Re-ran full end-to-end connectivity test after node1's restart to confirm ACL and forwarding persisted
